headline: Voyager 1 hits one light-day from Earth on November 18

sources.title: Voyager 1: What Is a Light-Day (NASA Science)

chunks.text: NASA said its Voyager 1 [[probe]] would set a new [[distance record]] on November 18, 2026. A probe is a space robot with no people [[on board]]. NASA said the probe would reach one [[light-day]] from Earth that day. That is the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 16 billion miles. Voyager 1 {{blasted off}} from Florida on September 5, 1977. It {{started out}} as a mission to study Jupiter and Saturn.

verbs.correct: To leave the ground on a rocket
verbs.wrong: To travel close to a planet
verbs.why: Rockets often blast off early in the morning. The crowd claps when a rocket blasts off. Voyager 1 blasted off from Florida on September 5, 1977.

verbs.correct: To be something at the beginning
verbs.wrong: To stop for a short rest
verbs.why: Many big companies start out in a garage. Her bakery starts out as a small hobby. Voyager 1 started out as a mission to study Jupiter and Saturn.

chunks.text: In 1990, Voyager 1 {{looked back}} and took a famous photo of Earth as a [[tiny dot]]. The sun sends a wind of tiny [[particles]] into space. This wind forms a giant [[bubble]] around the [[solar system]], the sun and its planets. In August 2012, Voyager 1 {{left that bubble behind}}. It entered [[interstellar space]], the space between the stars. Its trip has {{gone on}} ever since, at about 38,000 miles per hour.

verbs.correct: To turn and see what is behind you
verbs.wrong: To take a photo with a flash
verbs.why: Good runners rarely look back during a race. She looks back to wave at her mom. In 1990, Voyager 1 looked back and took a famous photo of Earth.

verbs.correct: To leave a place and not return
verbs.wrong: To protect a place from danger
verbs.why: Many people leave their small hometowns behind for big cities. Some families leave the busy city behind for a quiet farm. In August 2012, Voyager 1 left the sun's bubble behind.

verbs.correct: To continue for a long time
verbs.wrong: To move in a small circle
verbs.why: Some meetings go on for hours. The noise from the party next door goes on all night. Voyager 1's trip has gone on ever since, at about 38,000 miles per hour.

chunks.text: Because of the distance, a [[radio message]] from Earth now takes about a full day to reach the probe. Then the team waits about another day to {{hear back}}. Voyager's [[project manager]] gave an example. A "good morning" sent at 8 a.m. on Monday gets an answer around 8 a.m. on Wednesday. Large [[antennas]] on Earth {{pick up}} Voyager's [[weak signal]]. The probe {{sends back}} data very slowly. Engineers {{figure out}} each signal's travel time from the probe's speed and [[path]].

verbs.correct: To get an answer to a message
verbs.why: Job seekers often wait weeks to hear back. I usually hear back from my sister in a few minutes. The team waits about another day to hear back from Voyager 1.
Our car radio picks up a station from Canada at night. Ships at sea pick up signals from the coast. Large antennas on Earth pick up the probe's weak signal.

verbs.correct: To return data from far away
verbs.wrong: To count the stars in space
verbs.why: Weather satellites send back pictures of big storms. Space telescopes send back new images every day. Voyager 1 sends back data very slowly.

verbs.correct: To find an answer by doing math
verbs.wrong: To send a number by radio
verbs.why: Kids figure out the change at the store. My dad figures out the tip at dinner. Engineers figure out each signal's travel time from the probe's speed and path.

chunks.text: Keeping the probe working gets harder every year. Engineers have {{turned off}} its cameras and several [[instruments]] to [[save power]]. Scientists expect its power to {{run out}} in 10 to 15 years. Its twin probe, Voyager 2, should reach one light-day from Earth in November 2035. To mark the [[milestone]], NASA asked people around the world to {{join in}} by flashing lights at the sky after [[sunset]] on November 17.

verbs.correct: To stop a machine from working
verbs.why: I turn off the lights before bed. He turns off his phone at the movies. Engineers have turned off Voyager 1's cameras and several instruments to save power.

verbs.wrong: To be shared by two probes
verbs.why: Our milk runs out every Friday. A phone battery runs out fast in the cold. Scientists expect Voyager 1's power to run out in 10 to 15 years.

verbs.correct: To take part with other people
verbs.wrong: To pay a small fee online
verbs.why: Everyone joins in when the band plays that song. Neighbors join in to clean the park each spring. NASA asked people around the world to join in by flashing lights at the sky.

mainIdea.s: NASA said Voyager 1, a probe launched in 1977, would be the first object made by people to reach one light-day from Earth, on November 18, 2026. A message to it takes about a day.
mainIdea.why: Voyager 1 blasted off in 1977, and NASA said it would reach one light-day on November 18, 2026. A radio message now takes about a day to reach it.

mainIdea.s: NASA said an old spacecraft would pass the one light-day mark in deep space. Because it is so far away, engineers have lost all contact with it and can no longer send it any orders.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the team still talks to the probe. Messages are just slow, and antennas on Earth still pick up its weak signal.

mainIdea.s: NASA has launched a new probe that will try to reach the edge of the solar system by 2030. The agency says the craft is much faster than earlier missions and carries modern cameras.
mainIdea.why: Voyager 1 is not a new probe. It started out in 1977, and NASA said it would reach one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026.

tf.s: Voyager 1 is still traveling many years after it blasted off.
tf.why: It blasted off in 1977 and is still traveling.

tf.s: A radio message from Earth reaches Voyager 1 in about one hour.
tf.why: A message takes about a full day to reach the probe. Then the team waits about another day to hear back.

tf.s: Voyager 1 still sends back data to Earth.
tf.why: The probe sends back data very slowly, and large antennas on Earth pick up its weak signal.

tf.s: Voyager 1 is still inside the sun's giant bubble.
tf.why: Voyager 1 left that bubble behind in August 2012. It became the first spacecraft in interstellar space.

tf.s: Engineers turned off instruments to make the probe travel faster.
tf.why: They turned off its cameras and several instruments to save power. Scientists expect its power to run out in 10 to 15 years.

tf.s: NASA asked people to join in by flashing lights at the sky.
tf.why: To mark the milestone, NASA asked people around the world to join in after sunset on November 17.

lines.text: Did you hear that NASA said Voyager 1 would be one light-day from Earth on November 18?
One light-day? What does that even mean?
It's how far light travels in a day. That's about 16 billion miles.
Wow. That's [[a long way from home]].
Seriously? That thing was really [[built to last]].
It {{started out}} as a trip to Jupiter and Saturn, and the trip has {{gone on}} ever since.
Can they still talk to it?
Yes, but a message takes about a day to arrive. Then they wait another day to {{hear back}}.
Two days for one answer? That's slower than [[snail mail]].
Almost. It also {{sends back}} data really slowly.
Does everything on it still work?
Not everything. Engineers have {{turned off}} a lot of instruments to save power.
How much longer can it last?
Scientists think its power will {{run out}} in 10 to 15 years.
Keeping it alive must be [[a labor of love]].
I'm sure it is. NASA even asked people to {{join in}} by flashing lights at the sky.
What a nice idea. It deserves a party.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone or something is very far from where it began
ex: My cousin moved to Alaska, so she is a long way from home.
The lost dog was found a long way from home.

expressions.def: Made so well that it works for a very long time
ex: My grandma's old sewing machine was built to last.
These boots are built to last.

expressions.def: Letters sent by regular mail, which is much slower than email
ex: I sent the birthday card by snail mail.
Nobody uses snail mail for bills anymore.

expressions.def: Hard work that someone does because they care about it
ex: Fixing the old car was a labor of love for my dad.
The town garden is a labor of love for its volunteers.
